instructions: Lay out 4 slices of bread. Cover each with 2 slices of the kaşar, about 1 oz each, then top with the other 4 slices of bread.
Spread half the butter (1 tbsp) over the tops of the 4 sandwiches.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes. Put in 2 sandwiches, buttered side down, and press them flat with a spatula for the first minute.
Spread a quarter of the butter over the tops of those 2 sandwiches, then cook them for 3 minutes, until the bread is golden underneath.
Flip them and cook the other side for 3 minutes, until golden and the cheese has melted and stretches when you pull a corner apart.
Transfer them to a plate. Repeat with the remaining 2 sandwiches, spreading the rest of the butter over their tops and cooking them the same way.
Cut each sandwich in half and serve hot.
method_notes: Yemek.com's kaşarlı tost is bread, kaşar and butter pressed in a toastie maker until the cheese melts. This version uses a skillet pressed with a spatula, since most kitchens have no tost press. The only rated version found has one rating, so it is a fallback and RecipeTin Eats has no Turkish tost. Kaşar is sold at Turkish and Middle Eastern shops; kasseri or a mild provolone melts the same way. Sucuk and the other fillings of Ayvalık tost are left out to keep it the plain cheese tost.
